correctness.rationale: The logistic unitary sqrt(x(1-x)) f(x) yields exactly the causal exponential kernel 1_{r<s} exp[-(s-r)/2], so the commutator kernel has factor F(s)-F(r). Squaring gives the Hilbert-Schmidt double integral. For L=0, eventual decreasing v and fixed-displacement slow ratio give J(s)/v(s)^2-> integral_0^infty e^-t t²dt=2 by dominated convergence, making tail S2 equivalent to integral v². Frozen F_R has compactly supported integrable derivative and an explicit trace-class rank-one integral; Young bound controls error by 4 sup_{s>=R}v(s), proving compactness. For L positive finite, a translated weakly-null test yields nonzero oscillatory output; for L=infinity, monotone-phase integration by parts suppresses the oscillatory part while the nonoscillatory convolution remains nonzero. Power-chirp integrations give the two strict thresholds and logarithmic coefficient.
residual_risks: Requires eventual monotonicity/positivity; when v->0 assumes v(s+t)/v(s)->1. No S_p classification p!=2, no irregular oscillation speeds.
